You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

# miniserve - serve files and directories over HTTP

miniserve is a small command-line tool that serves files and directories over HTTP. It is intended for
quick ad-hoc sharing of files from a machine on a network.

Usage examples

Serve a directory:

    miniserve /path/to/directory

Serve a single file:

    miniserve /path/to/file.iso

Set a custom index file:

    miniserve --index index.html /path/to/directory

Serve a Single Page Application (forward non-existent paths to the SPA index):

    miniserve --spa --index index.html /path/to/spa

Require username/password:

    miniserve --auth user:password /path/to/directory

Start with TLS:

    miniserve --tls-cert /path/to/cert.pem --tls-key /path/to/key.pem /path/to/directory

Upload a file using curl (when upload support is enabled):

    # in one terminal
    miniserve -u -- .
    # in another terminal
    curl -F "path=@$FILE" http://localhost:8080/upload\?path\=/

For a full list of available options and flags, consult the tool's built-in help:

    miniserve --help

_miniserve() {

        cur="$2"
    else

    fi
    prev="$3"
    cmd=""

    do
        case "${cmd},${i}" in
            ",$1")
                cmd="miniserve"
                ;;
            *)
                ;;
        esac
    done

    case "${cmd}" in
        miniserve)
            opts="-v -p -i -a -P -H -S -O -c -d -q -u -U -m -M -o -R -r -g -z -C -D -t -l -F -W -I -h -V --verbose --temp-directory --index --spa --pretty-urls --port --interfaces --auth --auth-file --route-prefix --random-route --no-symlinks --hidden --default-sorting-method --default-sorting-order --color-scheme --color-scheme-dark --qrcode --upload-files --web-upload-files-concurrency --chmod --directory-size --mkdir --media-type --raw-media-type --on-duplicate-files --rm-files --enable-tar --enable-tar-gz --enable-zip --compress-response --dirs-first --title --header --show-symlink-info --hide-version-footer --hide-theme-selector --show-wget-footer --print-completions --print-manpage --tls-cert --tls-key --readme --disable-indexing --enable-webdav --size-display --file-external-url --help --version [PATH]"

                        oldifs="$IFS"

import re, pathlib, difflib
base=pathlib.Path("/tmp/variants/base_root.html").read_text()
def norm(t):
    t=re.sub(r'127\.0\.0\.1:\d+','HOST',t)
    return t
base=norm(base)
for p in sorted(pathlib.Path("/tmp/variants").glob("*_root.html")):
    if p.name=="base_root.html": continue
    t=norm(p.read_text())
    if t==base: print(p.name,"SAME as base"); continue
    print("\n===",p.name,"len diff",len(t)-len(base))
    # Use difflib on token-ish split by >< 
    a=base.replace("><",">\n<").splitlines(); b=t.replace("><",">\n<").splitlines()
    for line in difflib.unified_diff(a,b,lineterm='',n=0):
        if line.startswith(('+','-')) and not line.startswith(('+++','---')):
            print(line[:2000])
for name in ["qrcode","color"]:
    print("\nLOG/style",name)
    print(pathlib.Path(f"/tmp/variants/{name}.log") .read_text())
    a=pathlib.Path("/tmp/variants/base_style.css").read_bytes(); b=pathlib.Path(f"/tmp/variants/{name}_style.css").read_bytes(); print("style same",a==b,len(a),len(b))
    if a!=b:
        # find first diff
        for i,(x,y) in enumerate(zip(a,b)):
            if x!=y: print(i,a[max(0,i-100):i+300],b[max(0,i-100):i+300]); break

            total=0
            comps=row[1:]
            for i,v in enumerate(comps):
                if maskbits>>i &1: total+=v

import sys, os, subprocess, shutil, re
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from diffharness import S, norm

def setup(root):
    shutil.rmtree(root,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(root+"/sub/nested"); os.makedirs(root+"/other")
    open(root+"/existing.txt","w").write("old\n"); open(root+"/sub/inner.txt","w").write("inner")
def curl(s,args,path): return subprocess.run(["curl","-s","-i"]+args+[s.base+path],capture_output=True).stdout
def tree(root):
    out=[]
    for dp,dn,fn in os.walk(root):
        for n in sorted(dn+fn):
            p=os.path.join(dp,n); rel=os.path.relpath(p,root)
            if os.path.isdir(p) and not os.path.islink(p): out.append((rel+"/",None))
            else: out.append((rel, open(p,'rb').read() if os.path.isfile(p) else b''))
    return sorted(out)

def scenario(name,args,cmds,ready="/"):
    ress={}; logs={}; trees={}
    for label,exe in [("ref","/workspace/executable"),("mine","/tmp/myexe")]:
        root=f"/tmp/cmp_{label}"; setup(root)
        realargs=[a.replace("{ROOT}",root) for a in args]
        s=S(exe,realargs,ready=ready.replace("{ROOT}",root))
        res=[]
        for cargs,path in cmds:
            out=curl(s,cargs,path)
            # normalize root, port, date, temp paths
            txt=out.replace(root.encode(),b"ROOT").replace(f"127.0.0.1:{s.port}".encode(),b"HOST")
            txt=re.sub(rb'Date:.*?\r\n',b'',txt,re.I); txt=re.sub(rb'date:.*?\r\n',b'',txt)
            txt=re.sub(rb'\.tmp[A-Za-z0-9]+',b'.tmpXXX',txt)
            res.append(txt)
        ress[label]=res; trees[label]=tree(root)
        out,err=s.stop(); logs[label]=(norm(out,s.port,exe).replace(root,"ROOT"), norm(err,s.port,exe).replace(root,"ROOT"))
        logs[label]=(re.sub(r'\.tmp[A-Za-z0-9]+','.tmpXXX',logs[label][0]), re.sub(r'\.tmp[A-Za-z0-9]+','.tmpXXX',logs[label][1]))
    ok=True
    for i,(a,b) in enumerate(zip(ress['ref'],ress['mine'])):
        # normalize log timestamps not in curl output except Date header removed
        if a!=b: ok=False; print(f"DIFF {name} cmd#{i} {cmds[i]}\n ref {a[:800]}\n mine {b[:800]}")
    if trees['ref']!=trees['mine']: ok=False; print(f"TREE DIFF {name}\n ref {trees['ref']}\n mine {trees['mine']}")
    if logs['ref']!=logs['mine']: ok=False; print(f"LOG DIFF {name}\n ref {logs['ref']}\n mine {logs['mine']}")
    if ok: print("OK",name)

p=pathlib.Path("qrcode_penalty_test.go"); t=p.read_text()
# add zeroFormat helper (copy from earlier debug file logic)
helper='''
func zeroFormatG(grid [][]bool) [][]bool {
	g := make([][]bool, len(grid))
	for i := range grid { g[i] = append([]bool{}, grid[i]...) }
	size := len(g)
	coords1 := [][2]int{{8,0},{8,1},{8,2},{8,3},{8,4},{8,5},{8,7},{8,8},{7,8},{5,8},{4,8},{3,8},{2,8},{1,8},{0,8}}
	for _, cr := range coords1 { g[cr[1]][cr[0]] = false }
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ { g[8][size-1-i] = false }
	for i := 8; i < 15; i++ { g[size-15+i][8] = false }
	g[size-8][8] = false
	return g
}
'''
t=t.replace("func TestArasePenaltyChoices", helper+"func TestArasePenaltyChoices",1)
# In TestPenaltyVariants, variants loop currently uses penaltyVariant(g,vi). Add vi cases 8-11 in penaltyVariant function.
t=t.replace("	for vi := 0; vi < 8; vi++ {", "	for vi := 0; vi < 12; vi++ {")
# penaltyVariant switch add cases
t=t.replace('''	case 7: return araseL1 + l2*2 + l3rows + l3cols + l4floor
	}''','''	case 7: return araseL1 + l2*2 + l3rows + l3cols + l4floor
	case 8: return penaltyVariant(zeroFormatG(grid), 0)
	case 9: return penaltyVariant(zeroFormatG(grid), 2)
	case 10: return penaltyVariant(zeroFormatG(grid), 5)
	case 11: return penaltyVariant(zeroFormatG(grid), 6)
	}''')
p.write_text(t)

print('good',dict(good)); print('total',dict(total))
"
